Gem Quiz

Natural Born Beauty I May Not Be, But They Love Me Down in Texas

As an alternative to a traditional engagement ring, I’m hard to beat. Who am I?

Published

2 days ago

on

October 5, 2026

By

INSTORE Staff Instore October 2026 Issue
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:10
Instaread
  • Share
  • Tweet

LET’S COMPARE THE requirements for an alternative engagement gemstone:

Hardness: Check! (I’m an 8 on the Mohs scale)

Color: Check! A dazzling icy blue (OK, naturally I tend to be a little gray and bland but it’s nothing a shot of radiation can’t cure.)

Green credentials: Mostly small scale mining, no dictators supported

Provenance: International symbol of love? No, but I am the state gemstone of Texas. Don’t mess with Texas.

Price: Ha-ha! This is where I come into my own. At a few dollars a carat, that’s an awful lot of money left over to put toward a great setting, or the kids’ college education.

Who am I?

A Family Legacy, a Human Touch: Why Geiss & Sons Jewelers Chose Wilkerson for Its Going-Out-of-Business Sale

Geiss & Sons Jewelers is closing its doors. Co-owner Rose-Marie Geiss’s husband, Fernando Geiss, and his family opened the company’s first U.S. store in 1967 in The Promenade at Haywood in Greenville, South Carolina. Saying goodbye was emotional, but Geiss knew it was time. She looked at several companies for the going-out-of-business sale, and Wilkerson stood out. “Wilkerson was more human to us, and that’s why we chose them,” she said. What surprised her most was how involved the Wilkerson team was, handling the advertising and taking much of the headache off the family’s plate. Watch the story to see how Geiss & Sons Jewelers closed a family chapter with a partner it could trust.
